title: Spin out research-cli into its own repo (strategy B: vendor + drift-guard)
body:
research-cli's MVP was scaffolded inside the `agent-tools` umbrella at `tools/research-cli/`, hard-depending on the shared `agenttools_providers` + `agenttools_errors` packages and `lib/contracts/models.yaml` via a `sys.path` umbrella shim.

This issue tracks the spin-out into a self-contained repo using **strategy B (vendor + drift-guard)** — the proven task-cli pattern (task-cli#34/#37):

- Vendor `agenttools_providers`, `agenttools_errors`, and `models.yaml` under `vendor/`, each carrying a `# SYNC-HEADER` block with a pinned `CANONICAL_SHA256` + provenance commit.
- A `scripts/resync_vendored_libs.py [--check] <agent-tools>` drift-guard: `--check` fails on body drift (exit 1) vs infra error (exit >=2); bare run re-syncs.
- A pinned-SHA test (`tests/test_vendored_libs_sync.py`) that fails CI on local drift.
- A scheduled CI workflow that runs `--check` against the live agent-tools canonical and opens/updates a tracking issue on upstream drift.

Standalone acceptance:
- `research --help`, `research board`, `research ask --offline`, `research ask --json` all work from a clean checkout with NO agent-tools tree on `sys.path`.
- Tests + ruff green in this repo, including the vendor drift-check.

Strategy A (publish `agenttools-providers`/`agenttools-errors` to PyPI and depend on them) is deliberately deferred — it needs the CTO's PyPI account. When PyPI is provisioned, the vendored copies can be swapped for published deps.

title: SubprocessTransport.ask does not pass env= to subprocess.run (reachability/call desync)
body:
Carried verbatim from the agent-tools MVP source. `SubprocessTransport.is_reachable` resolves a key via `self.env` + `.env` files (the shared `KeyCascade`), but `SubprocessTransport.ask` runs the backend with `subprocess.run(..., shell=True)` and NO `env=`, so the child inherits `os.environ` instead of `self.env`.

Consequences:
- a key resolved from a `.env` file (not an env var) marks a seat reachable, but the subprocess env has no such variable, so a backend referencing `${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}` won't find it.
- an injected custom `env` (as in tests) is ignored by the real call.

Fix: pass `env=dict(self.env)` to `subprocess.run` (exporting keys found in `.env`), so reachability and the real call agree.

Found by the spin-out review (research-cli#1). Deferred from the spin-out PR to keep that change a pure relocation; this is a behavior fix on its own.

title: Non-editable pip install breaks manifest loading (vendor/contracts/models.yaml not packaged)
body:
`pyproject.toml` `packages.find` ships only the packages (`research_cli`, `agenttools_providers`, `agenttools_errors`); `vendor/contracts/models.yaml` is data, not a package, so a non-editable `pip install .` does not place it in site-packages. `default_manifest_path()` then points at a non-existent `site-packages/vendor/contracts/models.yaml`, and `research ask`/`board` without `--manifest` fail with `EXIT_USAGE`. Meanwhile `[project.scripts]` still creates the `research` console script, giving a false "it installed fine" impression.

The supported install paths today are the symlink install (`install.sh`) and `pip install -e .` (editable keeps the checkout so the vendored manifest resolves) — documented in the README. Fix options: ship the manifest as package data and resolve it via `importlib.resources`, or only expose the console script on the editable path.

Found by the spin-out review (research-cli#1).

title: research_cli/install.py file-mutation helpers are not unit-tested
body:
`research_cli/install.py` (the `install-skill` 3-layer installer) has nontrivial idempotent file-editing logic — `_replace_or_append_block`, `_strip_stray_markers`, `_inject_marked_block`, `_ensure_session_start_hook` (incl. the invalid-JSON / non-object-hooks / already-present branches) — and zero tests. A bug in the marker handling could corrupt a user's `CLAUDE.md` / `settings.json`. The `_replace_or_append_block` docstring even says "Pure … unit-testable".

Add unit tests for refresh/append/orphan-marker handling and the JSON-hook branches. (Logic is carried verbatim from task-cli's `install.py`, which is itself under-tested upstream — but this repo should cover its own copy.)

Found by the spin-out review (research-cli#1); README's coverage claim updated to point here.

title: transport: pass resolved provider key (incl. .env-only) into the backend subprocess
body:
## What is wrong
`SubprocessTransport.is_reachable()` marks a seat reachable when the provider key resolves via the CORE key cascade — which reads BOTH `self.env` and the `.env` files (`dotenv_files`, default `.env`). But `SubprocessTransport.ask()` runs the backend via `subprocess.run(..., shell=True)` with NO `env=`, so the child inherits only the parent process `os.environ` — neither the `.env`-resolved value nor `self.env`.

## User-facing consequence
A provider key present ONLY in a `.env` file (the documented `.env`-fallback install) makes the seat REACHABLE, so the engine selects it — then the live call fails at runtime because the backend reads e.g. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from an environment that never got it. `.env`-only installs are effectively unusable unless the user manually sources `.env` into every `RESEARCH_BACKEND_CMD`. A custom `self.env` is likewise honored by reachability but ignored by the call.

## Evidence
codex review on PR #5 (P2): transport.py — 'Pass resolved dotenv keys to the backend'.

## Acceptance criteria
- The backend subprocess sees the same provider key the cascade used to deem the seat reachable, including a `.env`-only key.
- `self.env` is honored by the call (not just reachability).
- A test proves a `.env`-only key reaches the backend (echo it back from the child).
- Existing transport tests stay green (PATH-dependent commands like `sleep` still resolve).

## Fix sketch
Extract a single `_resolve_provider_key(entry)` used by both `is_reachable` and a new `_backend_env(entry)`; `ask` passes `env=self._backend_env(entry)` — process env, overlaid with `self.env`, plus the resolved key injected under its canonical name when unset (env still beats the file, per the cascade).

title: Disable leftover SHIP_EXTERNAL_REVIEW via committed .ship-config
body:
## What
GitHub itself does not require an approving review to merge research-cli PRs, but gh ship still refuses a zero-review PR because the external-review gate defaults ON. The machine-wide env SHIP_EXTERNAL_REVIEW=0 is ignored after https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/624. Durable disable is a committed repo-root .ship-config with SHIP_EXTERNAL_REVIEW=0 on the PR base branch (https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/600, https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/pull/609). Evidence captured now: git show origin/main:.ship-config fails with path does not exist. Precedent: https://github.com/alex-mextner/tg-cli/commit/17431bf446dffd76016cf84704773a91806e93ba and merged https://github.com/alex-mextner/review-cli/pull/451.

## Why (motivation)
After https://github.com/alex-mextner/agent-tools/issues/624 the env off-switch no longer works, so gh ship came back to requiring a GitHub-side review even when branch protection does not. research-cli origin/main has no .ship-config, so every zero-review ship is refused.

## User impact
When you try to merge a research-cli PR with gh ship, the command refuses even though GitHub's merge button does not require an approval. You have to post a dummy GitHub review or wait for a Telegram hatch, so a solo ship that already passed review-cli quorum still cannot land.

## Cost of inaction
Every future research-cli ship stays blocked on a GitHub-side review that the repo policy already turned off, or burns a live Telegram hatch per PR.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] research-cli origin/main has a committed repo-root .ship-config whose only ship-gate line is SHIP_EXTERNAL_REVIEW=0. title: transport: stale os.environ canonical key can mask fresh alias/.env value in subprocess env
body:
## What
SubprocessTransport._subprocess_env() currently checks the merged child env (child.get(canonical), which includes inherited os.environ) before deciding whether to resolve/publish the canonical provider key via the cascade. It must instead check only self.env.get(canonical) - the same basis is_reachable() uses to decide a backend is reachable. When a stale canonical key (e.g. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) is already sitting in the parent process's os.environ, but the caller configured a fresh value under an alias (e.g. CLAUDE_API_KEY) or via .env, the merged child.get(canonical) check sees the stale value as 'already set' and skips re-canonicalization - so the backend subprocess receives the stale/wrong key even though is_reachable already reported the fresh alias as reachable. Fix: gate re-canonicalization on self.env.get(canonical) alone.

## Why (motivation)
Prior art: https://github.com/alex-mextner/research-cli/issues/2 and https://github.com/alex-mextner/research-cli/issues/6 (both closed) fixed the original desync between is_reachable's reachability decision and what the subprocess actually received. This is a follow-up regression in the same area: the fix introduced a new desync source (merged child env vs self.env) that reintroduces the same class of bug - seat selected as reachable, but the actual subprocess call can still receive the wrong key when a stale canonical value happens to already be sitting in the parent process's os.environ.

## User impact
A user/agent relying on an alias or .env-provided provider key can have research-cli confidently select a backend as reachable, then have the actual subprocess call silently use a stale/wrong key from os.environ instead - a confusing runtime failure (auth error, wrong-account response) that contradicts the reachability check that just passed.

## Cost of inaction
The is_reachable/_subprocess_env desync recurs any time a stale canonical env var is present in the parent process, regressing the exact bug class that https://github.com/alex-mextner/research-cli/issues/2 and https://github.com/alex-mextner/research-cli/issues/6 were meant to close, with no regression test guarding against it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] _subprocess_env() checks self.env.get(canonical), not the merged child env, before deciding to resolve+publish the canonical key — forced: transport.py:163-180 now gates re-canonicalization on self.env.get(canonical) alone (see PR #17 diff, research_cli/transport.py).
- [x] new regression test test_subprocess_transport_alias_beats_stale_os_environ_canonical passes: a stale ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in os.environ does not mask a fresh CLAUDE_API_KEY alias in self.env — forced: pytest tests/test_research_cli.py::test_subprocess_transport_alias_beats_stale_os_environ_canonical -v => 1 passed (worktree .worktrees/transport-stale-canonical, commit 062b321).
- [x] existing tests test_subprocess_transport_canonicalizes_alias_key_for_backend, test_subprocess_transport_env_var_beats_dotenv_for_backend, and test_subprocess_transport_child_inherits_process_env still pass — forced: pytest -k "canonicalizes_alias_key_for_backend or env_var_beats_dotenv_for_backend or child_inherits_process_env" => 3 passed (worktree .worktrees/transport-stale-canonical, commit 062b321).

title: chore(rig): enable worktree-only guard for the primary checkout
body:
## What
Enroll agent_hooks.worktree_only: true in rig.yaml so agents are forced to do feature work in git worktrees rather than editing the primary research-cli checkout directly, per [PR #13](https://github.com/alex-mextner/research-cli/pull/13).

## Why (motivation)
A dirty, diverged primary checkout (not a worktree) caused ship/review tooling failures for this repo; the worktree-only guard prevents recurrence.

## User impact
Agents and maintainers can no longer accidentally leave the primary checkout in a diverged state that breaks ship tooling.

## Cost of inaction
The primary checkout can drift from origin/main again, causing the same class of ship failures.
